name: DS18S20+
title: DS18S20 high-precision 1-Wire digital thermometer, 9-bit, -55 °C to +125 °C
summary: A temperature sensor that returns a 9-bit Celsius reading (0.5 °C per step) over a single-line 1-Wire bus, with ±0.5 °C maximum error between -10 °C and +85 °C. Each device carries a factory-lasered 64-bit ROM code, so many sensors share one bus wire and one controller. Two nonvolatile alarm bytes, TH and TL, let the controller find sensors whose last reading fell outside limits with an Alarm Search. The part runs from a 3.0 V to 5.5 V supply on VDD, or draws its power from the data line itself in parasite-power mode with VDD grounded. It comes in a 3-pin TO-92 and an 8-pin 150 mil SO.

circuits.title: Parasite-powered DS18S20 with strong pullup for conversions
circuits.description: The sensor runs with no supply of its own: GND and VDD both go to ground and DQ joins the 1-Wire bus, which a 4.7 kΩ resistor holds at VPU. A p-channel MOSFET driven from the controller connects the bus straight to VPU while a conversion or an EEPROM copy runs, carrying the up to 1.5 mA the sensor draws then. The bus continues to further 1-Wire devices.
notes: The MOSFET has to be on within 10 µs of a Convert T or Copy Scratchpad command and stay on for tCONV or tWR; nothing else may use the bus meanwhile.

circuits.title: DS18S20 powered from an external supply
circuits.description: The sensor takes its power on VDD from a separate supply, so the bus needs only its 4.7 kΩ pullup to VPU and remains free for other traffic while a conversion runs. GND goes to ground and DQ to the 1-Wire bus, which carries on to other devices.

operation.text: After power-up the sensor idles at low power. A Convert T (44h) command starts one conversion; the result lands in the two temperature bytes of the scratchpad and the device goes back to idle. The reading is in degrees Celsius, a 16-bit two's complement value with the sign extended, with 0.5 °C per LSB. With an external supply the master can poll with read time slots after Convert T: the device answers 0 while converting and 1 once finished. Under parasite power this polling is not available, because the strong pullup holds the bus high for the whole conversion.

After each conversion, bits 8 to 1 of the temperature register are compared with the 8-bit two's complement TH and TL bytes. A reading at or below TL, or above TH, sets the alarm flag; the flag is re-evaluated at every conversion, so it clears once the reading returns inside the limits. An Alarm Search (ECh) is answered only by devices with the flag set. After TH or TL are changed, a new conversion confirms the alarm state. TH and TL live in EEPROM and can serve as two general-purpose bytes when the alarm is unused.

With VDD tied to ground, the device draws power from DQ while the bus is high and stores charge on an internal capacitor, CPP, to ride through the low periods. That covers ordinary bus traffic within the specified timing and levels. A conversion or a scratchpad-to-EEPROM copy can draw up to 1.5 mA, more than the pullup resistor or CPP can supply, so the master switches the bus straight to the rail (a MOSFET) within 10 µs of Convert T or Copy Scratchpad and holds it there for tCONV or tWR = 10 ms, with no other bus activity. Above 100 °C, leakage may stop a parasite-powered device from communicating; an external supply is recommended there.
A supply on VDD removes the need for the MOSFET strong pullup, and the bus can carry other traffic during conversions.

The master sends Skip ROM (CCh), then Read Power Supply (B4h), then a read time slot. Any parasite-powered device pulls the bus low in that slot; externally powered devices leave it high. A low tells the master it must apply the strong pullup during conversions.
Each device holds a unique 64-bit lasered code: the 1-Wire family code 10h in the lowest byte, a 48-bit serial number, and a CRC of those 56 bits in the top byte.

The scratchpad is SRAM, with TH and TL backed by EEPROM. Bytes 0 and 1 (temperature LSB and MSB) are read-only. Bytes 2 and 3 reach TH and TL. Bytes 4 and 5 are reserved, cannot be written, and read as all ones. Bytes 6 and 7 are COUNT REMAIN and COUNT PER °C. Byte 8 is a read-only CRC over bytes 0 to 7. Write Scratchpad (4Eh) takes TH then TL, least significant bit of byte 2 first, and a reset before both bytes arrive can corrupt them. Read Scratchpad (BEh) returns from byte 0's LSB through byte 8; the master may stop with a reset at any point. Copy Scratchpad (48h) stores TH and TL into EEPROM; under parasite power the strong pullup must come on within 10 µs and stay at least 10 ms. Recall E2 (B8h) reloads them, reporting 0 while busy and 1 when done; the recall also happens by itself at power-up.

The ROM code's top byte is a CRC of its first 56 bits; scratchpad byte 8 is a CRC of bytes 0 to 7 and changes with them. The master recomputes the CRC from the received bits, shifted LSB first into a register cleared to zero, then shifts in the received CRC: a register of all zeros means the data arrived intact. The device does nothing itself on a mismatch; the master decides.

The single data line is driven by every device through an open-drain or three-state port and pulled up externally by about 5 kΩ, so the bus idles high. The DQ port has a typical 5 µA pull-down current source and an open-drain MOSFET marked 100 Ω. A transaction can pause indefinitely between bits as long as the bus is left high. Holding the bus low for more than 480 µs resets every device on it. Data and commands go least significant bit first. The device is always a slave.

Every access runs initialization (reset and presence), then one ROM command with its data, then one function command with its data; the device ignores a sequence with a step missing or out of order. After Search ROM or Alarm Search the master goes back to initialization. Skip ROM followed by Read Scratchpad is only safe with one slave, and Read ROM likewise; with several slaves their replies collide.

The master pulls the bus low for at least 480 µs, then releases it and listens. On the rising edge the device waits 15 µs to 60 µs and then pulls the bus low for 60 µs to 240 µs as its presence pulse.

Each write slot lasts at least 60 µs with at least 1 µs of recovery between slots, and starts with the master pulling the bus low. For a 1 the master lets go within 15 µs; for a 0 it holds the bus low for the whole slot. The device samples the line between 15 µs and 60 µs after the slot starts.

The device only sends data in read slots the master generates, right after Read Scratchpad or Read Power Supply, or after Convert T and Recall E2 to poll status. A read slot lasts at least 60 µs with 1 µs recovery, and starts with the master holding the bus low at least 1 µs then releasing it. The device leaves the bus high for a 1 or pulls it low for a 0, releasing it by the end of the slot. Its data is valid for 15 µs from the falling edge, so the master's low time, the rise time and its sample point together must fall inside 15 µs; margin is best with a short low pulse, a fast rise, and a sample late in that window.
